chunks: Glory be to Him from Whom is not hidden the blackness of dark dusk,
nor a gloomy night in the low parts of the earth,
nor on the high dim mountains that are adjacent,
and the thundering of clouds on the horizons of the skies,
and the sparking of lightning in the clouds,
and the falling of leaves blown away from their falling places by the winds of hurricanes or by downpour from the sky!
He knows where the drops fall and where they stay,
where the grubs leave their trails or where they drag themselves,
what livelihood would suffice the mosquitoes,
and what a female bears in its womb.
ai.seo_question: What aspects of creation demonstrate Allah's comprehensive knowledge in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Imam Ali’s sermon in Nahj al-Balagha illustrates the concept of 'Ilm al-Ghayb' (Knowledge of the Unseen), using a rhetorical progression from cosmic phenomena to microscopic details to affirm Allah’s absolute omniscience. In Shia exegesis, this detailed enumeration serves as a theological foundation for the infallible Imams' knowledge, which is derived from and reflective of Divine knowledge, thereby validating their authority in guiding the community until the appearance of al-Mahdi.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Glory be to Allāh from Whom neither the blackness of dark dusk
or of gloomy night (falling) in the low parts of the earth
is hidden, nor the thundering of clouds on the horizons of the skies,
nor the sparking of lightning in the clouds,
nor the falling of leaves blown away from their falling places by the winds of hurricanes or by downpour from the sky.
He knows where the drops. fall and where they stay,
where the grubs leave their trails or where they drag themselves,
what livelihood would suffice the mosquitoes
and what a female bears in its womb.
